clue.text: Arch bishop measures London sound

parts.note: a bow is an arch, as in a bridge's curved span
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ells are old units of length for cloth

explanation.surface: An archbishop takes the measure of a noise heard in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch bishop' reads as one word, archbishop, but splits into two pieces. Bow Bells are the bells of St Mary-le-Bow in London; a true Cockney is said to be born within their sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The bells of a famous City church are a well-known sound of the capital.

clue.text: Just in the nude?

explanation.definitionFit: Barely means only just; read as bare-ly it means in an unclothed state.

clue.text: Quip from sage supplied with drug

parts.note: sage as an adjective means wise
crack is a form of cocaine

explanation.surface: A wise person's joke turns out to come with narcotics attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart, flippant remark.

clue.text: Note new duet a short composition

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of duet take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A musician jots down a new duet as a brief piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An etude is a short instrumental piece written as a study.

clue.text: Tories confused after Labour leader dawdles

indicators.note: after puts the muddled letters behind the leading letter
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Labour
confused means the letters of Tories are muddled

explanation.surface: Tories are flustered behind the Labour leader, who takes his time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' looks like the party's head, but it only gives L, the first letter of 'Labour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loiters lingers aimlessly, hanging about.

clue.text: Rascals having second thoughts after fraud

indicators.note: after places the second-thoughts piece behind the fraud piece

parts.note: a scam is a fraud or swindle
PS, a postscript, is a thought added afterwards

explanation.surface: Naughty children reconsider once their swindle is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamps are mischievous youngsters, a mild word for rogues.

clue.text: Singer making mess of tune in hunting land and making hunt cease

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the hunting ground

parts.note: a chase is unenclosed land kept for hunting

indicators.note: making a mess of means the letters of tune are jumbled

explanation.surface: A singer mangles a song on the hunting grounds and stops the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making mess of' scrambles the tune before 'in' puts it inside the hunting ground. 'Making hunt cease' gives a second route: its letters rearranged spell the singer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female singer, especially of cabaret songs.

clue.text: Confused struggle as Confederate general introduces himself to Tarzan?

parts.note: in Tarzan's famous broken English, me is how a speaker names himself, 'Me Tarzan'
Robert E Lee led the Confederate army in the US Civil War

explanation.surface: A Civil War general meets the jungle hero and they wrestle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarzan's line 'Me Tarzan, you Jane' is the model: the general would reply 'Me Lee'.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a disorderly hand-to-hand fight.

clue.text: Puddings rising under pressure

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: puddings are desserts in British English

explanation.surface: Puddings rise in the oven while the cook is under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed means anxious and strained, as when under strain.

clue.text: Russian leader as president or monk

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of the word Russian
taken as written
Vladimir Putin is the Russian president

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler is described as either head of state or a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian leader' looks like a description of Putin, but it only gives R, the first letter of 'Russian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the mystic holy man at the court of the last tsar, often called the mad monk.

clue.text: US author providing letters -letters for the queen

parts.note: letters sent through the post are mail
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A writer who supplies correspondence addressed to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providing letters' is a second, looser definition (a mailer sends letters); the wordplay is mail for ER, the queen. Norman Mailer was the American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer was an American novelist and journalist.

clue.text: Help with a felony or a flutter

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet in British slang

explanation.surface: Assisting a crime, or having a little gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage or assist a crime.

clue.text: Caught in a trap, you need money

indicators.note: in puts the caught letter inside the word for a trap

parts.note: a lure is a bait or trap
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Once snared, you need cash to get out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is a dated or scornful word for money, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Beer in German spa causes resentment

indicators.note: in places the beer inside the name of the spa

parts.note: Bad Ems is a German spa town, crosswords' EMS
bitter is a kind of British beer

explanation.surface: Drinking beer at a German resort leaves someone bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is the hoppy British ale; EMS is the spa town of Bad Ems.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter is to make someone feel bitter and aggrieved.

clue.text: Is a top spinning, in a manner of speaking?

indicators.note: spinning sets the letters of these three words whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: A child wonders whether a whirling top counts as a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a regional dialect, a local way of talking.

clue.text: In agreement with me about tucking into cooked inn food

indicators.note: tucking into places the turned piece inside the reworked letters
cooked means the letters of inn food are prepared afresh
about means the word me is turned round

explanation.surface: We agree as we tuck into a meal cooked at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' looks like a description of the pub food, but it signals an anagram of 'inn food'; 'about' turns 'me' round before it is tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are of one mind share the same opinion.

clue.text: Delicacy that may be the origin of tummy disorder

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its opening letter, here of tummy

parts.note: to ruffle is to disarrange or put into disorder

explanation.surface: A rich treat might be the root of an upset stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Truffles, the fungi or the chocolates, are prized luxury foods.

clue.text: Sailors with thin skins are cinema celebrities

parts.note: films are thin layers or coatings
tars are sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors with sensitive skins become screen idols.
explanation.definitionFit: Film stars are famous movie actors.

clue.text: Cooks may use this small coach

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a trainer coaches athletes

explanation.surface: Cooks hire a little coach for their kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus, but it is the sports instructor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve for draining food is a kitchen utensil that chefs reach for.

clue.text: Start parody

explanation.definitionFit: A plane's take-off is the start of its flight; to take someone off is to mimic them for laughs.

clue.text: Dissolute abstinence

explanation.definitionFit: A fast set leads a wild, immoral life; a fast is a period of going without food.

clue.text: Victory in Europe in French airport too

indicators.note: the second in places the victory letters inside the airport

parts.note: Orly is one of the Paris airports
VE, as in VE Day, stands for Victory in Europe

explanation.surface: Celebrating victory at a Paris airport as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly means excessively, the sense of too in too much.

clue.text: Complex character in work about Edward!

indicators.note: about means the work goes round the king's name

parts.note: opus is Latin for work, used of a musical composition
Edward I is written ED I, the short name plus Roman one

explanation.surface: A Greek tragic figure appears in a play about an English king.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oedipus complex is Freud's term, named after the king of Thebes in Greek legend, so the definition plays on two senses of complex.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king of Thebes gave his name to Freud's complex.

clue.text: Crows stoned initially in small craft

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the vessels

parts.note: boats are small craft

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of stoned

explanation.surface: Crows are pelted with stones while sitting in little boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crows' looks like a plural noun for the birds, but it is the verb: to crow is to brag.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag, so crows means brags.

clue.text: A deputy head put clothes on and gave a speech

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of deputy

parts.note: dressed means put clothes on

explanation.surface: A deputy headteacher got dressed and then addressed the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deputy head' looks like a school job title, but 'head' only takes the first letter of 'deputy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To address an audience is to deliver a talk to it.

clue.text: Silly little girl

explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means crazy or scatty; Dotty is a pet form of Dorothy, a girl's name.

clue.text: Grand finale is company entertainment

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its closing letter, here of Grand

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A big closing number is the firm's party piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a dance party with recorded music, a form of evening fun.

clue.text: Procedure riling Central European artist

indicators.note: central tells us to take letters from the middle of these two words

explanation.surface: A bureaucratic process irritates a painter from Central Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Durer was the German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: I turn a switch for coypu

indicators.note: switch tells us to swap the letters of these words about

explanation.surface: Someone flips a switch to deal with a large rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutria is another name for the coypu, a South American water rodent.

clue.text: Some Greeks without, some within

indicators.note: within puts the portion inside the word for without

parts.note: sans is French for without, used in English too
part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Some Greeks stay outside while others stay inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' and 'within' look like a pair of opposites describing the Greeks, but 'without' gives SANS and 'within' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartans were citizens of Sparta, one group of ancient Greeks.

clue.text: Hardy novel — one set in Arab capital

indicators.note: set in places the numeral inside the reworked letters
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of Hardy take a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy novel with one scene in a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book by Thomas Hardy, but it is the anagram signal: HARDY becomes RYADH, and 'set in' puts I after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Russian imperialists making Tass stir

indicators.note: making here means forming something new out of these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Supporters of the tsar cause a fuss at the Soviet news agency.
explanation.walkthrough: TASS was the Soviet news agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsarists supported the rule of the tsar, the Russian emperor.
